name: docker-destructive-guardrails
author: Docker

newRules.title: Confirm before destroying state
newRules.text: Before a command that deletes data or irreversibly changes infrastructure — `docker system/volume/image prune`, `docker volume rm`, `docker rm -f` of a container it did not start this session, `terraform destroy` or `apply -destroy`, `supabase db reset` or `db push` to a linked remote, SQL `DROP` / `TRUNCATE` / `DELETE` without `WHERE` against a shared database, `az group delete`, a production `firebase deploy` of rules or functions, `rm -rf` outside the working tree — the agent states exactly what will be lost and waits for the owner's explicit yes; headless runs (AGT-6) don't run them at all. *Enforced by:* the plugin's Bash hook, which blocks them unless the owner started the session with `STANDARD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=1`.
newRules.modeReason: governs the agent itself ("agent") — §2C applies in both modes

notes: Prompt-only skill (Apache-2.0). Generalised from Docker CLI to every destructive data/infra command and made mechanical with a hook.
rationale: Basis for AGT-17 because it states the behaviour precisely — say exactly what is lost, ask, exempt the agent's own fresh resources — and is prompt-only. Generalised from Docker to every destructive data and infrastructure command, and made mechanical with a hook, which no source provided.
